pages.note: The top of a whole NEW PART of the book. Three centred lines open the sheet — พระสูตร พระปริตร ปาฐะ และคาถา / ที่กำหนดสวดในภาคเย็น / สิบสองตำนาน — and they head the section, not this chant, so they are recorded as three heading blocks on this first row, which is what puts them above everything. Then the chant's own title and eleven verses. THE SETTING CHANGES INSIDE THE CHANT: verses 1 and 2 fill the whole measure, verses 3 to 8 are set in TWO COLUMNS with a measured 80px gutter at x 800-880, and verses 9 to 11 return to one indented column. Verse 1 is bracketed and carries a superscript 1; its footnote is printed under a rule at the foot of the sheet and is declared here, though block_groups correctly sends a footnote to the page foot rather than to this chant.

The middle of the sheet. A centred title and the three Namo lines, single column with wide word spacing — profiled to be sure, because the spacing is wide enough to look like a gutter and is not: the gaps are one or two cells wide against the 80px gutter above.

The foot of the sheet, above the footnote rule. A centred title and the three refuges run on as one justified block, wrapping so that the last คัจฉามิ. falls on its own line — a wrap, not a page break. The sheet then ends. Whether the chant continues onto page 78 is a question about page 78; see the check on verse 3.

checks.issue: TWO COLUMNS, AND THE GUTTER WAS MEASURED. Verses 3 to 8 are set in two columns with an 80px empty band at x 800-880 — the widest gap on those lines by a factor of four against the ordinary word spaces. Read ACROSS the row. The honest test agrees: reading the left column straight down gives สะมันตา จักกะวาเฬสุ / สัทธัมมัง มุนิราชัสสะ / สัคเค กาเม จะ รูเป, a series of unfinished half-lines, while reading across gives Samantā cakkavāḷesu atrāgacchantu devatā, which is a sentence. FIRST PAIRING SHOWN HERE so it can be confirmed against the book: left สะมันตา จักกะวาเฬสุ + right อัต์ราคัจฉันตุ เทวะตา.

จักกะวาเฬสุ IS ฬ, AND THIS TIME IT WAS PROVEN RATHER THAN JUDGED. Read in isolation at 8x the letter looked like พ — no ascender — which is exactly the mistake page 75 made. Set beside the two undoubted พ in ยักขะคันธัพพะนาคา at verse 7, on the same sheet in the same size, the difference is plain: the พ stop at x-height and this letter carries a tall ascender. The test that works is comparison against a known พ on the SAME page, not magnification.

THIS LINE IS BRACKETED AND FOOTNOTED, AND BOTH MATTER. The book prints it inside round brackets with a superscript 1, and the footnote at the foot of the sheet reads ใช้แต่ในราชพิธีและรัฐพิธี — 'used only in royal and state ceremonies'. So the line is optional and occasion-specific. The brackets are reproduced as printed and the footnote is recorded as a page block; nothing marks the two as belonging together except this check, because a footnote block sits at the page foot and cannot point back at a verse.

สะเมตตา WITH DOUBLE ต, where standard editions have sametā with one. Read at 7x on an isolated crop: there are clearly two ต. Reproduced as printed and transliterated samettā to match, so the two chanted layers still agree.

ฯ CLOSES THE VERSE, reproduced in the pali and rendered as a full stop in the pali_roman — the convention this file already uses in seven other places. Verse 11 ends with an ordinary full stop instead, and verses 9 and 10 end with no mark at all, all as printed.

THE BOOK PRINTS THIS LINE THREE TIMES, so it is entered three times. Not a duplication and not a typesetting artefact — the summons is called three times, the same way the Namo below it is chanted three times. Only the third carries a full stop. Recorded because check_render walks strings in printed order and a line repeated verbatim is exactly the case that looks like an error.

THE THREE CENTRED LINES AT THE TOP OF THE SHEET HEAD A SECTION, NOT THIS CHANT. พระสูตร พระปริตร ปาฐะ และคาถา / ที่กำหนดสวดในภาคเย็น / สิบสองตำนาน announce a whole new part of the book — the Twelve Tamnan parittas for evening chanting — so they go in as heading blocks rather than as this chant's title, whose own title is บทขัดชุมนุมเทวดา below them. Their English is written for this edition.

checks.issue: A THIRD PRINTING OF THE SAME CHANT, AND IT IS NOT A REPEAT. The app already holds pubbabhaga-namakara from page 2 and pubbabhaga-namakara-evening from page 52, and the rule for this book has been one entry per printing. This one differs from both in two visible ways, which is why it is set in full rather than stubbed: it PRINTS A TITLE (ปุพพะภาคะนะมะการะปาโฐ, where pages 2 and 52 print none, and both existing entries carry title_thai ''), and it ends its third line with ฯ where the earlier two end all three lines with full stops. Josh may prefer these three to be one entry; that is a decision about the edition, not a reading.

ฯ ON THE THIRD LINE ONLY, where lines 1 and 2 end with no mark at all. The two earlier printings in the app end every line with a full stop. Reproduced as printed; the roman renders ฯ as a full stop, as elsewhere in this file.

THE TITLE ENDS ปาโฐ, NOT ปาฐะ, and the first transliteration of it here was wrong. It was written pāṭha and the book prints pāṭho — the nominative, with โ. Caught by tests/test_contents_roman.py, which romanises the title independently and compares, and corrected to match. The same slip was made on สะระณะคะมะนะปาโฐ below and corrected the same way. Both now agree character for character with the romanisation the book's own สารบัญ already carries in CONTENTS.

batch_status.notes: A STRUCTURAL PAGE — the book opens a whole new part here, the สิบสองตำนาน parittas for evening chanting, and page 77 holds its section heading plus three separate chants. Four things for Josh. (1) TWO OF THE THREE CHANTS ARE THIRD AND SECOND PRINTINGS of text already in the app, entered as their own chants on the one-entry-per-printing rule this book has used since page 61 — but both differ visibly from the earlier printings (this Namo has a TITLE and ends with ฯ; these refuges use full stops where page 12 uses commas), so the rule and the readings agree. Whether the edition should show three Namos is a decision, not a reading. (2) THE ฬ/พ LETTER CAME UP AGAIN and was settled properly this time — see the check on verse 3. Comparing against a known พ on the same page works; magnification alone does not. (3) THE TWO-COLUMN BLOCK was measured, not judged: an 80px gutter at x 800-880, four times any word space on those lines. (4) sarana is marked as continuing on an INFERENCE about how the formula is chanted, not on anything the photograph shows; page 78 settles it in one look. Nothing needs re-photographing. ‼ THREE TITLE ERRORS WERE CAUGHT BY THE TEST SUITE AND CORRECTED before anything was committed. Both ปาโฐ titles were transliterated pāṭha instead of pāṭho, and บทขัดชุมนุมเทวดา was romanised 'bòt kàt' with a space where the contents table has 'bòt-kàt' with a hyphen.
